title: EgoAgent Product Code Agent controlled acceptance campaign

comparisons.title: Governed evolution during seven recurring releases
comparisons.interpretation: Both solve all releases. Treatment pays an intentional learning cost and creates, repairs, verifies, then hot-loads a reusable Skill; this pair establishes the learning event, not immediate cost savings.

comparisons.title: Fresh-session transfer using the evolved Quasar Skill
comparisons.interpretation: Both solve all transfers. The treatment discovers and directly invokes the previously evolved Skill in each fresh task instead of re-reading, rewriting and re-testing the normalization logic.

comparisons.title: Core execution versus global Library reuse after publication
comparisons.interpretation: Both solve all transfers. Any compatible Identity can discover the globally published Skill, confirming interface/implementation separation. This replicate cuts tool calls but costs more model tokens and time because the comprehensive Flow still plans and reviews every turn; simple tasks should be routed to Core.

comparisons.title: Durable workspace memory across fresh trajectories
comparisons.interpretation: The fact is never written to a project file and the second step starts a fresh trajectory. Only the memory-enabled Flow retrieves the exact synthetic rollback code.

comparisons.title: Passive token-pressure compaction over 25 noisy turns
comparisons.interpretation: Both preserve four exact durable facts. The clean post-fix treatment triggers one compaction and reduces total tokens by 26.9%, but provider uncached input is 10.0% higher in this replicate; compaction controls working-context size and total spend, not deterministic prefix-cache behavior.

comparisons.title: Frequent proactive curation over 15 noisy turns
comparisons.interpretation: Both are correct, but repeated model-authored history rewrites destroy provider prefix-cache locality and increase cost. This negative result motivated the production Flow's new minimum-context gate.

comparisons.title: One large repair with and without an isolated child Agent
comparisons.interpretation: Both pass all twelve tests. Delegation cleanly isolates disjoint packages and reduces primary-Agent context, but does not reduce total tokens at this task size; it is a context-isolation mechanism, not a universal cost optimization.

comparisons.title: Core versus Full Flow on a small one-shot repair
comparisons.interpretation: Both pass all five tests. No reusable capability, memory, compaction, evolution or delegation benefit is available, so Full pays discovery and independent-review overhead. This is direct evidence for routing small one-shot repairs to Core.

comparisons.title: Matched large-observation repair with model-facing pruning off/on
comparisons.interpretation: Both repair the same roughly 50KB source and pass. The treatment preserves the contract-bearing head and bug-bearing tail in working context, keeps the exact full read once in the trajectory, and sharply reduces subsequent model input.

standalone.title: Latest full product Flow on a six-stage release engineering task
standalone.interpretation: The v24 product Flow completes all six stages while exercising discovery, passive compaction checks, component-owned repeat guards, tool-output pruning, durable memory, checkpoints, transactional change review, independent quality/safety reviews and an evolution review.

standalone.title: Latest production Flow after making the repeat-guard component reachable
standalone.interpretation: The v24 Flow passes a real five-check dual-subsystem repair after hidden exact-call rejection is disabled in favor of the visible 2/3/5 component policy. No reminder fires on this normal run; deterministic fault injection separately proves the reminder path is reachable.
